subject.title: [Bug] web_fetch fails in dual-stack networks when DNS returns IPv6 special-use addresses

question: Should OpenClaw relax the default SSRF DNS-answer rule so mixed result sets can proceed after dropping blocked candidates, or keep the current any-blocked-answer fail-closed rule?
rationale: The code change is small, but the behavior is a default outbound SSRF policy decision and should reflect maintainer security intent rather than an automated guess.

options.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
options.body: Allow the request only when at least one resolved address is allowed, remove blocked candidates from pinned lookups, and cover mixed/all-blocked cases in tests.

options.title: Keep any-blocked fail-closed
options.body: Treat polluted mixed DNS answers as intentionally blocked and document trusted proxy or fake-IP range configuration as the supported workaround.

options.title: Make mixed-answer behavior opt-in
options.body: Preserve the current default and add or reuse an explicit operator-controlled policy for polluted DNS environments.

recommendation.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
recommendation.body: Allow the request only when at least one resolved address is allowed, remove blocked candidates from pinned lookups, and cover mixed/all-blocked cases in tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The file history points to this person as the strongest recurring owner of the SSRF policy and net-policy boundary involved in the decision.
